Either collapses C to a free-text synthesizer over incident notes.

label: Zero-holes cross-stack correlation, during the incident, at scale
kill_criterion: Correlation completeness or false-linkage rate on a live, multi-source, partially-degraded incident is too low to produce a defensible timeline; the 'zero-holes' promise fails exactly when the estate is under attack.
test_that_resolves_it: Replay 3 historical multi-source incidents through the correlation logic; measure evidence-chain completeness and false-linkage rate against the known ground truth.

label: MSPs actually USE it DURING the incident, not after (the wedge)
kill_criterion: MSPs run C after the fire is out (post-hoc), not during. The 'live' differentiator evaporates and C is a report generator wearing a live badge - which is the ticket-RCA card already in the build.
test_that_resolves_it: Contextual inquiry on actual current IR workflow at 3-5 MSPs (the mini-council's shared blind spot - no one observed real IR practice), then a wizard-of-oz live-RCA session under simulated incident pressure to see if it is used during.
evidence: [?] North Star ~50% use-during, explicitly flagged behavior-untested.

label: An MSP trusts an AI mid-incident enough to act on its live correlation
kill_criterion: Under acute stress (2am, adrenaline high, breach active), the senior tech defaults to human judgment and ignores/bypasses the AI until the incident is resolved, voiding the 'during' value.
test_that_resolves_it: Same simulated-incident operator session as C-LIVE; observe whether the tech acts on the AI's live output or falls back to the on-call human. Collapses into one study with C-LIVE and C-SOLN.
evidence: [A] - no evidence any MSP will hand live incident reasoning to an AI; incident-response culture is human-trust-based. SDT (mini-council Voice 3): autonomy threat is sharpest under time pressure.

label: An AI-authored RCA is admissible / insurer-acceptable / not a catastrophic liability when relied upon
kill_criterion: Insurers or auditors will not accept an AI-generated RCA as the reliance document without a licensed human examiner's attestation, OR a wrong AI-authored RCA relied upon in a claim/litigation creates severe multi-party liability. Either makes C an input to a human's report, not 'the artifact the insurer requires'.
test_that_resolves_it: Legal scoping (admissibility, discoverability of model reasoning, spoliation risk) + 2-3 cyber-insurer conversations: will you accept an AI-generated RCA as the reliance document, or require a human forensic examiner sign-off?
evidence: [?] - offering DESIGNS for reliance ('defensible by morning, the artifact the insurer requires') but never scopes admissibility. EU AI Act 2026-08-02, compliance owner <TBD> (offerings doc). C-specific and potentially fatal to the headline value prop.

label: Demand is for THIS mechanism (live AI-authored RCA), not just the destination (a fast defensible RCA)
kill_criterion: MSPs want the outcome (a fast, defensible cross-stack RCA) but reject the mechanism (an AI correlates and drafts it live while you approve) - they want a human SOC to hand them the report, not an AI to babysit mid-crisis.
test_that_resolves_it: Solution-fit operator session presenting the live-AI-RCA mechanic; observe whether it matches how they actually want the incident job done. Collapses with C-LIVE and C-TRUST.
evidence: [A] CS:MEDIUM - all demand data measured desire for the outcome; never for this mechanism. Independent survey VALUE rating is soft (3.13) even while ranked #3 priority.

kill_criterion: Demand proves an artifact of the shared 8-person qual base, or softens further under independent quant; the soft 3.13 value-rating is the true signal, not the #2/#3 ranking.

label: No account/claim-ending wrong-RCA event and no admissibility failure
kill_criterion: A wrong AI-authored root cause is relied upon by a client/insurer/court; the reliance-chain liability lands on the MSP and possibly N-able. Asymmetric and unrecoverable - a wrong RCA loses a claim, not just an account.
test_that_resolves_it: Bundled with C-LIABLE legal scoping; define confidence-tiering carried into the client/insurer-facing artifact and a mandatory human-attestation gate before any relied-upon output.
evidence: [?] - reliance-chain liability unexamined; C-specific because the output is designed to be relied upon by an adversarial third party.

label: A 2am reliability / uptime bar and degraded-mode design exist
kill_criterion: C is down, slow, or blind at the moment of an active incident - especially when the incident itself has degraded the network/identity/endpoint telemetry C reads from. Failure is correlated with the event C exists to handle.
test_that_resolves_it: Define an incident-grade SLA + degraded-mode behavior (what C does when its own data source is compromised); chaos-test correlation under simulated telemetry loss.
evidence: [?] - operational SLA unscoped; the failure mode is structurally correlated with the incident, the nastiest kind.

label: The alert-to-RCA trigger does not false-fire into erosion
kill_criterion: C fires RCAs on false-positive alerts, burning cost, creating possibly-discoverable 'we had an incident' artifacts, and training the MSP to ignore its triggers; OR it waits for human confirmation and is no longer 'during' for the early phase where speed matters.
test_that_resolves_it: Define and test trigger logic against a labeled alert stream; measure false-trigger rate and downstream mute behavior.
evidence: [?] - the trigger dilemma (auto-fire vs wait-for-human) is unnamed in the offering; the sibling 'Alert Flood Suppressor' default exists precisely because alerts are noisy.

kill_criterion: Huntress/Blackpoint/CrowdStrike fold live-RCA narration into their managed SIEM/MDR where they already own the telemetry and staff a 24/7 human SOC - delivering a human-defensible report that is strictly safer for the liability job than an AI-authored one.
